If models are "LXC DN15 R40" etc., then q3 is model-level too technically. Both representations are valid. Let me decide: Option A (all model_level): 8 attributes × 33 values. Option B (hybrid): model_level for q1, q2, q3_over_q1 (33 each); config_level for nominal_diameter, q3, q4, length, connection_type with axis "nominal_diameter" (3 conditions each). Option B is more compact and semantically clean. But config_level per schema: "attribute, axis, values[]: {condition, value}". Values with {condition, value, unit_symbol}? The rule 5 says values follow same structured form: {condition, value, unit_symbol}. OK. I'll go with Option B. And matrix_tables hold the full per-DN tables. Model list: 33 models with model_id "LXC DN15 R40" ... and label maybe "DN15, Q3/Q1 = 40". Keep attributes {} empty or minimal? I could include attributes: {"nominal_diameter_mm": 15, "q3_m3h": 2.5...} but that duplicates config_level. I'll include minimal attributes or none. The schema shows models[] entries with just model_id in the example. I'll add label with the human-readable variant, and leave attributes empty/null? I'll include attributes with the per-model values — no wait, that's heavy duplication again. Example R137 shows models without attributes. I'll include model_id and label only. Hmm, actually including per-model attributes{} would make each model self-contained which is nice for downstream. But 33 models × ~8 attrs again duplicates. I'll follow the example: model_id + label. Actually let me add attributes to models too — the schema defines attributes{} in models and it makes each model self-contained. It's duplication but machines can handle. Hmm. The R137 example omitted attributes. I'll include a few key attributes per model: q1, q2, q3, q4, q3_over_q1, nominal_diameter. You know, I think I'll include them — more useful, no rule against. But it makes JSON huge. Let me estimate: 33 models × 6 attrs ≈ 200 lines. Plus model_level 3×33=99 lines. Plus config 5×3=15. Plus matrices 3×11 rows=33 rows. It's large but acceptable. Hmm, I'll strike a balance: models[] with model_id, label, and attributes {nominal_diameter, q3_over_q1, q1, q2, q3, q4}. model_level: q1, q2, q3_over_q1 matrices. config_level: nominal_diameter-related (q3, q4, length, connection_type, nominal_diameter). matrix_tables: 3 tables. Wait, if models have attributes AND model_level has q1/q2 matrices AND config has q3/q4 — triple duplication for some. Let me simplify: models[] = {model_id, label} only (like the example). model_level = q1, q2, q3_over_q1. config_level = axis "nominal_diameter": nominal_diameter (value 15/20/25 mm), q3, q4, connection_type, length. matrix_tables = 3 flowrate tables. Clean, no duplication. Now characteristics.type_level — value objects must be {value, unit_symbol, unit_id, footnote_markers}. The schema shape: "
